about: A web panel for managing Nginx, the program that sits in front of many websites and serves their pages.

prs.title: Site list sorts by number
prs.broken: Clicking the number column in the site list did nothing; the order stayed as the files were read.
prs.changed: The list now sorts by that column.
prs.matters: Sites can be ordered the way the column promises.

prs.title: Quieter logs at start-up
prs.broken: Every start filled the log with "record not found" messages for lookups that are expected to miss.
prs.changed: Those expected misses are no longer logged.
prs.matters: Real problems are easier to spot in the log.

prs.title: Maintenance mode keeps shared settings
prs.broken: Putting a site into maintenance dropped settings other sites share, so nginx refused to start.
prs.changed: Maintenance mode now keeps those shared settings.
prs.matters: Turning on maintenance for one site no longer breaks the others.

prs.title: Log lines with a spaced user name show up
prs.broken: Requests from a user name with a space never appeared in log search or on the dashboard.
prs.changed: The log reader now handles names with spaces.
prs.matters: No requests go missing from the logs.

prs.title: Notes in a site's settings survive a save
prs.broken: Notes at the end of a settings line were thrown away when a site was saved in the panel's block editor. Certbot, the common certificate tool, adds one to every line it writes, so those sites lost them all.
prs.changed: The editor now keeps those notes. Most move to their own line just above the setting, and inside page rules they stay on the same line.
prs.matters: Saving a site in the panel no longer quietly strips the notes people and tools left in it.

prs.title: A site under maintenance can't be deleted or renamed by mistake
prs.broken: A site in maintenance mode shows visitors a 'down for maintenance' page. Deleting or renaming it left that page on under the old name, and with the site gone from the panel, nobody could turn it off.
prs.changed: The panel now refuses to delete or rename a site while it is under maintenance, and says why. The delete check was already meant to do this but looked in the wrong folder.
prs.matters: Visitors are not left stuck on a maintenance page that nobody can switch off.

prs.title: A renamed site keeps its certificate renewing
prs.broken: The panel links a certificate to its site's file name. Renaming a site left the certificate on the old name, so automatic renewal skipped it. Nothing warned anyone, and the certificate just ran out.
prs.changed: Renaming a site or a stream now moves its certificate to the new name too.
prs.matters: Renaming a site no longer quietly lets its HTTPS certificate expire.

prs.title: Downloaded PFX certificates open in OpenSSL 3 and Node
prs.broken: The panel's PFX download used an old 40-bit cipher that OpenSSL 3 and Node refuse by default. The file downloaded fine but could not be opened there.
prs.changed: The download now uses the format the library recommends for wide support, which Windows and IIS still import.
prs.matters: A certificate exported from the panel works in current tools without extra flags.
